title: Compliant and still blind: What Article 72 monitoring doesn't see
headline: Why EU AI Act Article 72 monitoring misses behavioral drift
summary: Many organisations are preparing Article 72 post-market monitoring plans for the EU AI Act, treating them as administrative compliance paperwork rather than active governance disciplines. This compliance-driven focus often targets performance metrics like accuracy and error rates, which fail to detect quiet behavioral drift in production models. As a result, systems can satisfy technical performance targets while gradually shifting how they operate and make decisions.
why_it_matters: Organisations designing post-market monitoring must look beyond standard performance thresholds and compliance files to track behavioral drift, ensuring their AI systems do not quietly evolve away from what leadership expects.

quotes.text: The trouble is that many organizations risk designing Article 72 monitoring primarily around performance failure: accuracy dropping, error rates rising, complaints piling up. These plans are not designed to catch behavioral drift.
A system that behaves differently from the one leadership thinks it has is a governance problem, but it is also a business problem.

classification.significance_reason: Provides valuable practitioner commentary on the limits of standard compliance monitoring under the EU AI Act, applicable to international AI governance practices.
